turns.content: Hydroboration of a conjugated diene with bulky chiral Ipc2BH gives one observed product over a range of temperatures. Which mechanistic possibilities should be compared to explain that result?
Contrast a stepwise electrophilic addition through an equilibrating allylic cation with concerted H/B delivery. Why can temperature redirect the former between 1,2- and 1,4-addition products?

Apply that contrast to the diene/Ipc2BH reaction. What best explains the absence of temperature-dependent product switching, and what compatible role might reagent sterics or facial selectivity still play?
Why are syn addition and stereospecificity alone insufficient to prove formation of a single constitutional product?
State the best-supported explanation while retaining appropriate uncertainty about the unisolated contribution of Ipc2BH steric and facial selectivity.
Give a concise final account of why the reaction yields one product across the tested temperatures.
